summary: Conventions: proposed_change is NONE on every row (the Refuter proposes no edits) and word_delta is therefore 0 throughout; is_deletion mirrors whether the REVIEWED change is a deletion. THE HEADLINE: all seven of the lead's own proposals fail ARCH-B - not one of L1-L7 states a second-order consequence or a rollback, so by the review's own gate every one is a suggestion, not a change. Four of the seven are also killed on merits. L6 is the most dangerous item on the slate: it amends GAUNTLET §0, a §1-PROVEN rule, to admit a CONTRACT label in src/config/ as evidence - the exact artifact class this review measured as systematically unreliable four separate times (skills.ts grading a HUD readout CONTRACT and manufacturing two more numbers from it; chi.ts asserting an absence of evidence its own kickoff had contradicted two days earlier; src/config/CLAUDE.md:6 advertising a label gate no test implements; mobs.ts citing the ledger to keep a placeholder). L1 deletes an owner rule the owner re-confirmed three times, going further than C61, C68 and C75 all did on the same evidence, on a circular argument. L3 deletes 62 words of rationale and is the precise failure C56 predicted one row later - it destroys the text that made D6 knowable, and C33 achieves the same correction by REPLACING. L7 names L1 as the immediate chop: the largest lane on the board, gated by R1 on a permission grant whose evidence directory contains nothing but a README, when C102's skilldata port is 20x smaller with a proven template and no legal gate. L4 is instance-not-class housekeeping that C54 fixes at the mechanism. L5 bundles two unrelated edits whose evidence supports only one; C83 and C55 file them separately and better. OF THE 102 LENS FINDINGS: 41 are suggestions, not changes (missing 2nd-order and rollback); 6 propose nothing; and of the ~55 complete proposals, roughly 25 survive. FIVE CLUSTERS DOUBLE-COUNT: four rewrites of §3.5 (adopt C58's deletion), four of R2/ordering (adopt C99), four of §7 (adopt C61, the only one that leaves the owner's rule to the owner), four of §2.1 (adopt C98, the only one that preserves the android-v0.682 caveat), and four incompatible remedies for the SESSION-LOG rule (adopt none as filed). C57/C71/C77/C99 bill roughly 107 words of ARCH-E savings against about 55 words of actual text - any synthesis that sums them overstates its budget by ~100 words. TWO STRUCTURAL PROBLEMS WITH THE REVIEW'S OWN GATE: ARCH-B is incident-shaped, so it deletes the whole Margin of Safety lens by construction (C74 - 8.2 GB single-copy corpus whose loss retroactively voids 1,696 verdicts); and C40 verifies that walls #1-#4 and #7 have no record anywhere in the repo, so the 'eleven walls, zero data lost' claim shielding §1 is auditable for six, not eleven. THE FIVE THINGS WORTH DOING, in order: C65/C84 (archive the permission evidence - five minutes, discharges an undischargeable ship gate), C102+C78+C91 (port skilldata.xml with its build caveat - the actual chop), C37 (gate L0-C reads a file no script writes and that does not exist on disk), C80 (t2 judges at width 1 on a heavy lane; 701 of 1,696 verdicts rest on one critic), C30 (a test for the handoff rule that has now failed twice in 24 hours). Everything else is map.
